arborescence: Implement solve(n, edges, root) for minimum-weight directed spanning arborescence rooted at root. Each edge is (u,v,weight), including parallel edges and negative weights. Return minimum integer cost or None if impossible. n may be 200, m 10000, so enumeration is not acceptable; implement cycle contraction correctly, including nested cycles.
circulation: Implement solve(n, edges) for minimum-cost feasible directed circulation with lower/upper capacities. Each edge is (u,v,lower,upper,cost), with integer nonnegative bounds and signed costs. Return optimal integer cost, or None if infeasible. Account for disconnected negative-cost cycles and nonzero lower bounds; conserve flow at every vertex. n <= 40, m <= 200, capacities <= 30. Avoid enumerating edge flows.
steiner: Implement solve(n, edges, root, terminals) for minimum-cost directed Steiner subgraph connecting root to every terminal. Each edge is (u,v,weight), weights nonnegative; shared edges count only once. Return integer minimum cost or None if impossible. n <= 80, m <= 500, <= 9 terminals; use a subset-DP plus shortest-path approach, not edge-subset enumeration.
extensions: Implement solve(n, edges) to count exact topological orderings / linear extensions of directed constraints. Each edge is (u,v). Duplicates must not change the result. Return 0 for any cycle, including self-loops. Handle n <= 22 within a few seconds using subset DP, not permutations. Return an exact Python integer.
